decisions.summary: Narrowed the publish_log card-number check so it stops withholding entries that merely contain a long identifier.
decisions.rationale: The card pattern matches any 13-19 digit run, and Jules session ids are 19 digits, so three consecutive decisions were withheld from the public operations log for mentioning a session id. That log is a graded deliverable and the withholding was silent, because failing closed is the design and nobody was reading the exit code. The check now requires the Luhn checksum AND a major-industry-identifier of 3-6, which every payment card issued by Visa, Mastercard, Amex or Discover has and which arbitrary numeric identifiers do not. Luhn alone was insufficient: the session id in question passes it. This narrows precision, not coverage.
decisions.evidence: Three withheld entries traced to session id 1652844863819652924; publish_log exit 30 before the change and exit 0 after; tests cover Visa, Mastercard, Amex and Discover still matching.
decisions.falsifier: If a real payment card ever appears in the public log, this was narrowed too far and the leading-digit check is the part to reconsider first.

No model can win that race. The seven application files were new to main and conflicted with nothing, so they were re-landed unchanged on a fresh branch. Commission Jules to stop logging user-supplied image filenames. app/main.py line ~152 logs f"Successfully processed image '{image.filename}' ..." at INFO, which writes a user-controlled string into Cloud Run logs. The image bytes are already handled correctly (in-memory only, EXIF stripped, never persisted) and no question text is ever logged, so this filename is the single path by which a user's own words reach durable storage. A filename can itself carry personal data (for example 'uppehallstillstand_anna.jpg'), which CHARTER.md's personal-data rule covers. Fix: log the fact of the upload without the name -- size and content type are enough for debugging. This is not hypothetical: as of 2026-08-11 the product has its first real user, an exchange student in Lund, so any image she uploads exercises this path. open_questions.question: XPRIZE rules may restrict or require particular Google AI services (possible Vertex AI clause). Re-verify against the current rules page before the submission narrative claims which services were used. HANDOFF.md section 2 already says to re-verify the rules summary before submitting.
open_questions.answer: Resolved 2026-08-11 by reading https://xprize.devpost.com/rules directly. There is no Vertex AI clause. Section 4 states two requirements verbatim: 'A Project must use at least one product from Google Cloud' and 'Projects that include LLM functionality must use the Gemini API for at least one LLM call in the deployed application.' The Gemini Developer API (generativelanguage.googleapis.com) is the Gemini API and satisfies the second; Cloud Run satisfies the first outright, and the Gemini API additionally bills as a Google Cloud service under project Undra. The deployed app calls Gemini in app/main.py, which is the clause's 'in the deployed application' and was a deliberate design decision on 2026-08-06. No migration to Vertex is required or advantageous. Do not re-open without new rule text.

The free tier returns identical wording for 'model not on your tier' and 'too many requests per minute', and that string had been listed as a permanent marker. Fixed in commit 258c8e2: only a depleted prepaid balance is now treated as permanent, calls are paced at 4.5s to stay under ~15 RPM, and the API's own RetryInfo delay is honoured. Cycle #5 then completed cleanly on gemini-3.6-flash under the same conditions. The model is available; treat this question as closed and do not plan around it.

open_questions.question: Devpost submission requires revenue broken out by May/June/July/August, with related-party revenue disclosed separately. Three of those months are structurally zero (the business did not exist). Confirm how to state that honestly without it reading as an omission — the ledger has no rows for those months because there was nothing, which is different from unmeasured.
open_questions.answer: Resolved 2026-08-11. The rules ask verbatim for 'Revenue by Month. Revenue broken out by calendar month: May, June, July, and August 2026.' The honest answer is $0 for all four, with one sentence of fact: Undra did not exist before 2026-08-03 and its first commit is dated 2026-08-05, so there was no business to earn revenue in May, June or July. The hackathon period opening on 19 May does not imply the project existed then. NOTE for whoever writes the submission: this question is exactly what produced the fabrication on main. The form demands a breakdown for months that predate the project; the drafter had nothing to enter and invented a narrative ('local infrastructure setup and operational charter design phase') to make correct zeros look deliberate. State the zeros and state why. Do not explain them. Marketing spend is $0 and the rules require it disclosed even when zero.

open_questions.question: jules_file_task tool call returned HTTP 400 (Unknown name 'autoPr' at 'session') when attempting to file a task. Need to re-try or report to Operator if persistent.
open_questions.answer: Fixed 2026-08-06. The autoPr field was added to runner/jules.py the previous evening to stop finished Jules sessions stranding as unsubmitted patches, but it is not a field this API accepts — autoPr, autoPR, auto_pr, automaticPullRequest and createPullRequest are all rejected as unknown names, so the whole request 400'd. Removed. Stranding cannot be solved from the API (there is no submit endpoint either); a completed session with no PR needs a human to click Publish, and jules_task_status now says so.

open_questions.question: Future improvement, not urgent: switch GitHub Pages from legacy branch-deploy to a GitHub Actions build-and-deploy workflow. Today the ops loop commits rendered docs/ to main every cycle, which is what let a long-lived feature branch collide with generated output. With an Actions deploy the site is uploaded as an artifact, so docs/ need never be committed at all. The catch: the site is rendered from ledger.db, which lives only on the lab box, so the workflow would have to regenerate it from the committed reports/ledger-dump.json instead — publish_log.py currently reads sqlite, not the JSON dump. Deferred 2026-08-07: the legacy build is healthy (7 of last 7 runs green, site current) and the deadline is the binding constraint. Operator's idea.

app/main.py hardcodes its Gemini model as a default rather than reading models.work from invariants.toml, which AGENTS.md #5 requires. The default was gemini-2.5-flash, which returns 404 'no longer available to new users', so the deployed service answered every permitted question with an error while the refusal path kept working — a failure invisible to anyone who only tested a refusal. Worked around on 2026-08-07 by setting UNDRA_APP_MODEL on the Cloud Run service and pinning it in cloudbuild.yaml. The proper fix is for the app to read the model from configuration, so a model retirement is a config change rather than a silent outage.
open_questions.answer: Worked around 2026-08-07 and verified: UNDRA_APP_MODEL=gemini-3.6-flash is set on the Cloud Run service and pinned in cloudbuild.yaml, and the deployed app now answers permitted questions from the model. The question stays worth acting on — the model is pinned in two places rather than read from invariants.toml — but it no longer blocks anything.
